dedupe_keys.name: google data centre power usage effectiveness fleet pue

description: This page reports the power usage effectiveness (PUE) of Google's global fleet of large-scale data centres, the ratio of total facility energy to the energy used by IT equipment. Contents: the 2025 trailing-twelve-month fleet average of 1.09, a claim of 83 percent less overhead energy than the industry average, an explanation of the measurement boundaries, and the statement that compute delivered per unit of energy rose more than threefold in five years. Producer: Google, measuring the whole worldwide fleet continuously across all seasons and including all sources of overhead, once a site reaches stable operation. Coverage: Google's own large sites worldwide, not the wider industry. Access: an HTML page with charts, no download link seen on the page read. Licence and cost: free to read; no reuse licence is stated. Caveats: the data are self-reported, aggregated across the fleet with no site-level values, and the industry comparison relies on the Uptime Institute survey cited in a footnote. Simulation uses: a benchmark for cooling and power-overhead assumptions in data centre energy demand and capacity-planning models, useful for bounding best-case overhead. It relates to the DeepMind cooling control case study (case_study-deepmind-google-data-centre-cooling-control) in the catalogue.
